newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia wool test volume slightly up - AWTA.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia wool test volume slightly up - AWTA.

text.p: Australian Wool Testing Authority Ltd has tested 1.1 percent more wool in the first four months of the 1996/97 season than in the previous corresponding period, spokesman Peter Morgan said in a statement.
The quality of superfine wool tested was the same as for the equivalent period last year, a drought year, he said.
This implied that superfine woolgrowers had maintained production despite significant declines in superfine wool prices, he said.
The quantity of wool tested for length and strength had risen to 79 percent of all combing wool, up from 72.8 percent last year, he said.
Vegetable matter content was averaging two percent, up from 1.6 percent, reflecting better seasonal conditions, while mean fibre diameter had strengthened marginally to 22 microns, he said.
While staple length was slightly shorter, staple strength was stronger nationally but marginally weaker in Queensland, South Australia (SA) and Western Australia (WA), he said.
There were wide differences in the quantity of wool tested from different states compared with last year, with Tasmania, Victoria and New South Wales up but Queensland, WA and SA down.
